scenes.headline: How an autoencoder learns to forecast its own latents
scenes.sub: One Gaussian per step, in a space it shapes itself
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Thumper! Autoencoders compress images well, but sampling from them gives mush. This paper fixes that with one small change.

scenes.text: Replace the fixed standard normal prior with a forecast: each latent's prior is predicted from the latents before it.
scenes.mark: predicted from the latents before it
scenes.say: Stop scoring every latent against one fixed bell curve. Predict each latent's prior from the latents before it.

left.title: Causal VAE
left.say: A standard prior samples every token independently, which scrambles how neighbours fit together.

right.title: EVA
items: Each token scored against a forecast
right.say: Here the prior reads the earlier latents, so sampling walks the same chain the data does.

steps.say: The encoder sees the whole image at once.
It gives every position a Gaussian, and we draw a latent from each.
A causal decoder reads them left to right and rebuilds each token.
The same hidden state also forecasts the next latent, through two small linear heads.
A divergence term pulls forecast and posterior together.

scenes.title: The term that changed
scenes.say: One term in the bound changed.

parts.say: On the left, where the encoder put this latent.

parts.note: prior: a forecast from earlier latents
parts.say: On the right, the forecast from latents already drawn.

steps.say: Plain regression collapses to the mean. A three part mixture breaks past three modes.
The latent models find every cluster. The forecast keeps samples on them.

items.say: The decoder forecasts the next latent.
Draw it from that Gaussian, the only randomness.
The decoder reads out the token.
Then repeat, one cheap pass per position.

scenes.label: ImageNet FID, causal VAE to EVA, same backbone
scenes.note: the forecast heads are 0.11% of the weights
scenes.say: On ImageNet the quality score falls from a hundred to under eight, for a tenth of a percent more weights.

scenes.text: Make the latent predictable, and a single Gaussian per step is enough; the decoder supplies the modes.
scenes.say: Ask the encoder for latents that are predictable, not just compact. Then one Gaussian per step is enough.

recap: The encoder learns to be predictable
The decoder turns one Gaussian into many modes
scenes.say: A prior that forecasts, an encoder that cooperates, and a decoder that supplies the modes.
